title: Excel Sheet Column Number
summary: Given a string columnTitle representing an Excel sheet column title, return the corresponding column number.
statement: Given a string columnTitle representing an Excel sheet column title, return the corresponding column number. For example, A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26, AA=27, AB=28.
constraints: The label contains 1–7 uppercase English letters and represents a column from 1 through 2^31 - 1 (A through FXSHRXW in column order).
A=1, …, Z=26. Each additional letter shifts previous positions by a factor of 26; this is not a sum of letter values.
hints: A letter's contribution depends on its position in the label.
Read from left to right; each new letter multiplies the previous value by 26.
Start at zero and update value = value×26 + (letter-'A'+1) for every letter.
editorial: The running value represents the entire prefix already read. Appending a letter shifts that prefix one position and adds the new one-based digit. The oracle independently sums explicit powers of 26 from right to left. Boundary cases distinguish one- and multi-letter labels, and the maximum label maps exactly to 2147483647, safely representable by the browser's JSON number format.

tests.explanation: A is the first column, so its number is 1.
